blindSummary:
Nothing relating to being trans is criminalised in this country; a national LGBTI action plan (2021-2027) is in force (implementation is admittedly flawed), and a UN independent expert on sexual orientation and gender identity conducted a full country visit in July 2024 - a sign of government openness unusual for the region. The capital hosts an annual Pride.

For a visitor: no legal exposure, no bathroom laws, no documented police targeting; the realistic risk is social hostility outside the capital and in more conservative rural areas. Candidate status for membership of a supranational union is driving slow alignment.
blindOutOfScope: The LGR gap and action-plan implementation gaps are resident-facing.
blindSourceSummaries: End-of-mission statement of a UN independent expert on SOGI after the 1-12 July 2024 country visit (the capital plus five municipalities). Assesses implementation of national and international standards on violence and discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity; notes cooperation from the government and identifies challenges and good practices.

A regional LGBTI-rights organisation's annual review 2024 (covering 2023), chapter on this country. Documents hate violence against trans people and sex workers (ten cases reported), LGBTI people's limited access to state services due to discrimination (civil society filling gaps with food packages, bill payments, reimbursement of documentation costs for IDs and passports), education barriers (30% of LGBTI respondents unable to complete compulsory education), and successful discrimination complaints.

Full report to the UN human-rights council (June 2025) of the UN independent expert on SOGI following the visit to this country. Evaluates the country's adherence to human rights standards for LGBT people, examines the situation of lesbian, gay, bisexual and gender-diverse persons in depth, and makes recommendations on violence and discrimination.

LGBTQ+ news outlet (Feb 2010): this country passed an anti-discrimination law covering sexual orientation (but not same-sex marriage); homosexuality carried a 10-year sentence until 1995; welcomed by local gay-rights groups and a regional LGBTI-rights organisation as a regional example.

National daily (2021): an MP of a major opposition party called LGBT awareness meetings in capital high schools 'groups with a dubious agenda' and 'revolting' - example of anti-LGBT political rhetoric in this country.

National daily (2021): another politician of the same party called LGBT school meetings a 'terrible scandal' and claimed an 'LGBT government' was favouring the community in housing, education and employment - example of hostile political discourse.

Regional reporting outlet (Oct 2011): this country's anti-discrimination commissioner reprimanded a ruling-party MP for saying in parliament that 'homosexuality is disease and should be treated with hormones' - the commissioner urged parliament to guarantee LGBT community participation; homosexuality decriminalised in 1995.
blindLocalsOnly: There is no legal gender recognition (this country rejected a self-ID recommendation at its UPR) - a resident-facing gap that does not affect a foreign passport holder.
blindTangential: No SOGI hate-crime statute, and discrimination in key areas drew concern from the parliament of a supranational union - relevant mainly to visitors who experience or witness bias incidents.
